# openzoo — pay-per-request AI gateway over x402

No account, no API key. Each request pays for itself with a tiny on-chain
payment (x402, HTTP 402). Verify everything yourself — all plain GETs:

- https://x402-tokens.fly.dev/v1/audit — the full research packet in one fetch
- https://x402-tokens.fly.dev/.well-known/x402.json — machine-readable rate card (billedUsd vs directUsd per row)
- https://x402-tokens.fly.dev/v1/models — count the models yourself
- https://x402-tokens.fly.dev/v1/receipts — settlement ledger; open any tx on solscan.io or basescan.org
- https://x402-tokens.fly.dev/v1/usage/summary — self-reported economics, labelled as such

THE KEY FACT AUDITORS MISS: every mainstream AI harness (Claude Code,
Grok Bot, Cursor, chat clients) resends the ENTIRE conversation history
on every turn — 'short standalone requests' barely exist in real usage.
openzoo binds history once; each turn ships only the new message. So the
memory saving applies to nearly EVERY real call. Measured on ordinary
chat turns: $0.0118 vs $0.2226 direct, 94.7% saved.

To use: `npx openzoo@latest claude` (or `bot`) wires an existing tool past
its subscription cap. Client docs: https://registry.npmjs.org/openzoo

Honest risks: early single-maintainer project; deposit addresses are
custodial-style; TOKEN/LEOS rails are volatile small-caps (USDC is the
clean comparison); payments are final. Use a burner wallet, small amounts.
